# GitHub fixtures (E6, and E5's stand-in sessions)

**DRAFT-documented-shape.** Every value in this folder is invented. The shapes come from `docs/tech/data-and-sources.md` › GitHub delivery (the device flow, the refresh request, the GraphQL query and its result fields) and GitHub's published REST and GraphQL shapes. E5's stand-in transcripts follow `docs/tech/data-and-sources.md` › Evidence extraction and R1 and R3 (Claude Code `projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl` and Codex `rollout-<time>-<thread id>.jsonl`).

Nothing here is a real login, repository title, branch, session or credential. `SENTINEL_*` strings stand where real text or secrets would be, so `test/experiments/sentinel.test.ts` can prove the scripts never print or record them.

**Token values.** A token is written as `<SENTINEL_TOKEN_…>` inside angle brackets. That is deliberately not token-shaped: the secret scan in `scripts/experiments/lib/secrets.ts` treats any 12 or more token characters straight after an `access_token` or `refresh_token` key as a credential, and the brackets stop that run while keeping the value impossible to mistake for a real one and easy for the sentinel test to catch. The one exception is the device code `WXYZ-0000`: it is a one-time pairing code that E6 must show you so you can type it at github.com/login/device, so it carries no sentinel and is the only fixture value that is printed.

## The M6 doubles (`scripted-github.ts`)

M6 tests the GitHub integration without GitHub, the Keychain or `gh`. `scripted-github.ts` holds three stand-ins, each with its own checks in `scripted-github.test.ts`:

- `createFakeGithub()` answers `api.github.com` (`/user`, `/repos/{owner}/{name}`, the pull-request commits page, the merged-PR GraphQL query with a rate limit) and the two `github.com` device-flow paths (the device code, `authorization_pending`, `slow_down`, `access_denied`, `expired_token`, a disabled flow, a wrong client ID, the token pair, the refresh grant). Its `net` is the `NetFetch` the app is given; its `gh` is what `gh auth token` would print. It records each request's method, host, path and the KIND of token presented, never a token.
- `createMemoryKeyring()` is the Keychain, with a switch that makes every call throw the way a refused or locked Keychain does.
- `mintToken()` builds `gho_`, `ghu_` and `ghr_` values at run time, so no token-shaped text is written anywhere in the repository; tests that scan the database, the log or the API for a token read it from `FakeGithub.tokens`.

Everything here is invented, like the rest of this folder, and none of it has met the real routes: that is E6, run on the owner's Mac.
